label: text
text: Replying to Mr. Ramsay MacDonald, Leader of the Opposition, regarding the matter, Mr. Chamberlain said that the memorandum appeared to be a copy of a document of which another American newspaper gave an account two months ago. label: text

label: text
text: The Z�ovieff letter was the notorious document in which Moscow gave instructions to British Communists to arrange an armed rising on England. A copy of this letter was said to have leaked out of the Foreign Office. The Labour Party chimed that it was a forgery, but its authenticity has been generally accepted. TRAIN DASHES INTO CHAR-
A-EANC TRAILER.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Berlin, May 11.

label: text
text: The Basle express dashed into the trailer of a char-a-banc at a level crossing at Rothmalsch between Heidelberg and Carlsruhe, killing eleven people and injuring five.

label: text
text: The victims were male choristers going home after winning a prize in a local competition.

label: text
text: The char-a-bane got, clear but the trailer was smashed-to-match-wood.

label: text
text: The disaster was due to a signal-man omitting to close the gates.

Moscow May 11

label: text

label: text
text: Peking, May 11.—The Japanese aeroplanes flying to Peking are expected to leave Tokyo on the 23rd and to arrive on the 26th. They are due to return on the 28th. — Reuter.

label: text
text: Peking, May 10.—The students' delegates, who failed to see Tunn Chi-jui yesterday, were seen by his aide-de-camp, who promised them that Lu Ching-Jin, Commandant of the Precautionary Force, would see them on Monday and give them a reply from the Government. Pending this reply, the students are not agitating to-day, but the police are still taking precautions. It is reported in judicial circles that five of the arrested students have been released on bail.—Reuter.

label: text
text: CHEERING THRONGS.

label: text
text: Marshall von Hindenburg, Germany's hero during the war, is the nation's idol again, judging from the welcome he received in Berlin yesterday.

label: text
text: FETED IN BERLIN.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Berlin: May 11."

label: text
text: A triumphal welcome was given to Marshal von Hindenburg this afternoon on his formal entry into Berlin to assume his duties as President.

label: text
text: As the train from Hanover drew "to the gaily beflowered suburban station of Heerstrasse, nine aeroplanes hovering overhead dropped flowers.

label: text
text: The President, who was wearing a top hat and frock coat but no medals, was welcomed by the Chancellor. Dr. Luther, the chief Burgomaster of Berlin and other notable personages, with all of whom he shook hands silently.

label: text
text: THE OLD MAN AIR

label: text
text: After the presentation of a bouquet by Dr. Luther's young daughter, Marshal von Hindenburg left for the Chancellor's palace. The 5-mile route was lined the whole way by cheering crowds which von Hindenburg acknowledged. Nationalist organisations were very prominent, but the Republicans adhered to their earlier boycott decision.

label: text
text: Throughout the drive von Hindenburg exhibited the air of an old man well pleased with the cordiality of his reception.

label: text
text: At the conclusion of the drive the crowds dispersed quietly the Monarchists marching off singing patriotic songs.

label: text
text: To-night the President dines with the Chancellor. He takes the oath to-morrow.

label: text
text: Marshall von Händenburg in a statement before his departure for Berlin, earnestly pleaded for unity.

label: text
text: He said that he would bear in mind those who were "poor and distressed and would try to act as peace-maker. His aim was for a happy Fatherland.

label: text
text: As the train started amid the strains of “Deutschland Ueber Alles, von Hindenburg called for three cheers for Germany. The crowd enthusiastically responded.
